intentMappings.intent: Combine calendars without copying or merging ownership
intentMappings.coverage: Existing substantive answer; expand rather than new route
intentMappings.usefulAddition: Add a fifth connection type: an external service that creates destination records. Show one original work meeting and one masked personal copy; an overlay itself creates neither.

intentMappings.intent: Block work availability for private commitments without revealing details
intentMappings.coverage: A genuinely distinct task is absent as a worked workflow; adjacent ownership/privacy principles already exist
intentMappings.usefulAddition: First expand existing route with viewing versus publishing availability. A future standalone guide would need provider-specific busy/free semantics, what invitees actually see, directional field review and a disposable test. It must explicitly distinguish manual blocks from verified automation.
intentMappings.cloudBoundary: No verified automatic cross-provider busy-block replication, masking or exclusion rules in this batch. Do not advertise them.

intentMappings.intent: Duplicate original and synced copy appear in one view
intentMappings.usefulAddition: Trace original versus generated copy and the service that created it. Hiding a row is not deleting a destination copy; disabling a replication rule may have service-specific cleanup effects. Do not recommend deleting invitations or assuming all apps detect clone records.

intentMappings.intent: Microsoft shared calendar missing versus readable but not writable
intentMappings.coverage: Existing canonical is brief and needs substantive replacement; no new near-duplicate route
intentMappings.usefulAddition: Distinguish personal Outlook account, organisational account, shared owner calendar and room/resource. Diagnose identity, accepted share, read permissions, destination edit access and approved app connection. Google missing-calendar instructions are not universal Microsoft instructions.
intentMappings.requiredBeforeAuthoring: Read current Microsoft support/Graph permission documentation and inspect actual Cloud Microsoft shared/resource support. Do not generalize CalendarBridge integration requirements.

intentMappings.intent: Sync historical or far-future events, or use sync as backup
intentMappings.coverage: Existing backup/search intents; useful caveat instead of new article
intentMappings.usefulAddition: Ask whether a third-party replication service has a date window before treating its destination as a complete archive. Separate missing history from wrong account or search scope.

intentMappings.intent: Stop copying private events into another account safely
intentMappings.coverage: Potential distinct task, but permission revocation and generated-copy cleanup must not be conflated
intentMappings.usefulAddition: Future provider/service-specific workflow should inspect who created destination records, whether disconnect removes copies, which account retains originals, and other invitations or exports already distributed. Start as a clearly separated section; no generic deletion recipe.

currentBodyFindings: Existing sync, work/personal and disagreement routes already give useful ownership, hiding, permissions and diagnostic distinctions.

Older Exchange text attributes refused connections usually to policy and makes a running-cost claim; these are unsupported by this research and should be removed or separately substantiated during revision.

Older combined-view route says every account editable in place and Google sync never requires payment; this is overbroad around permissions and perpetuity, and has stale tier prose. Research does not authorize or perform correction.
boundaries: Publisher bodies establish what those publishers document, not measured product performance or Cloud capabilities.
No search volume, Google position, exhaustive keyword access, ranking improvement or ChatGPT recommendation/citation evidence collected.
No automated cross-provider event copying, clone masking, managed resource support or clone suppression claimed for Cloud Calendars.
No new page recommended merely for a keyword variation.
No raw competitor prose copied; no independent security audit or privacy guarantee.
